title: God Finishes His Work and Makes a Home for People

verses.1: God finished making the heavens and the earth and everything in them.
verses.2: On the seventh day He was done with all His work, so He rested.
verses.3: God made the seventh day special and set it apart as holy, because that was the day He rested from everything He had made.
verses.4: This is the story of how the heavens and the earth were made. When the LORD God made them,
verses.5: there were no bushes or plants growing yet because the LORD God had not sent any rain, and there was no one to take care of the ground.
verses.6: But water would come up from the earth and water the surface of the ground.
verses.7: Then the LORD God formed a man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
verses.8: The LORD God planted a garden in a place called Eden in the east, and He put the man there to live.
verses.9: The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow in the garden — trees that were beautiful and good for food. Right in the middle of the garden was the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.10: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided into four rivers.
verses.11: The first river was called Pishon, and it flowed through the land of Havilah where gold is found.
verses.12: The gold there was good, and there was also bdellium and onyx stone.
verses.13: The second river was called Gihon, and it flowed through the land of Cush.
verses.14: The third river was called Hiddekel, and it flowed east of Assyria. The fourth river was the Euphrates.
verses.15: The LORD God put the man in the garden to take care of it and watch over it.
verses.16: The LORD God told him, "You can eat from any tree in the garden.
verses.17: But do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. If you eat from that tree, you will die that very day."
verses.18: Then the LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper alongside him."
verses.19: The LORD God had formed all the animals and birds from the ground, and He brought them to Adam to see what names he would give them. Whatever Adam called each living creature became its name.
verses.20: Adam gave names to all the livestock, the birds, and the wild animals — but for Adam there was not found a helper alongside him.
verses.21: So the LORD God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. While he was sleeping, the LORD God took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
verses.22: The LORD God formed a woman from the rib He had taken from the man and brought her to him.
verses.23: Adam said, "This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She came from man, so she will be called Woman."
verses.24: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
verses.25: The man and his wife were both naked, but they were not ashamed.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
